title: Early Mechanical Insufflation-Exsufflation in Mechanically Ventilated ICU Patients (FREE-BREATH)
official: Early Use of Mechanical Insufflation-Exsufflation to Improve Weaning Efficiency in Mechanically Ventilated Critically Ill Patients: A Randomized Controlled Trial (FREE-BREATH)
summary:
Cough insufficiency is one of the main complications in critically ill patients undergoing mechanical ventilation, whether invasive or non-invasive. This impairment is multifactorial, involving both mechanical factors (endotracheal intubation, reduced expiratory muscle strength) and neurological/systemic factors (delirium, sedation, ICU-acquired weakness), leading to ineffective bronchial clearance, secretion retention, atelectasis, respiratory infections, and an increased risk of weaning failure and reintubation.

Mechanical Insufflation-Exsufflation (MI-E) is a cough augmentation technique that simulates the physiology of a natural cough by alternating positive and negative pressure, generating a forced expiratory flow that promotes bronchial clearance. While historically used in neuromuscular disease populations, more recent evidence suggests it may also improve secretion clearance in intubated critically ill patients.

This single-center, prospective, randomized controlled trial (no drugs or medical devices under investigation as the intervention device is already approved and in routine clinical use) aims to determine whether early use of MI-E (within 72 hours of intubation) reduces the overall duration of invasive mechanical ventilation by preventing early secretion accumulation and improving weaning efficiency. Secondary aims include the impact on the number of therapeutic bronchoscopies, respiratory complications, and length of hospital stay.
conditions: Mechanical Insufflation-exsufflation Session ( With Cough Assist)
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients ≥18 years of age
* Invasive mechanical ventilation
* Clinically significant bronchial secretions (≥1 suctioning event per hour in the preceding 24 hours)

Exclusion Criteria:

* Contraindications to MI-E (bullous emphysema, subcutaneous emphysema, undrained or suspected pneumothorax, pneumomediastinum, recent barotrauma, tracheoesophageal fistula) (Breas Medical 2022; Respironics 2012; Chatwin 2023)
* Known neuromuscular disease
